posts.caption:
If your leads are spread across spreadsheets, WhatsApp chats and sticky notes, deals slip away quietly.

Episode 2 of Zoho Explained looks at Zoho CRM: lead capture, one timeline per customer, a deal pipeline, workflow automation, reports and forecasts, and Zia, Zoho's AI assistant. It also connects to Campaigns, SalesIQ, Desk and Books.

Zoho says more than 350,000 businesses use it, with 1,200+ integrations (zoho.com/crm, Nov 2026).

Next episode: Bigin, Zoho's simpler CRM for small teams.
posts.title: Zoho CRM explained | Zoho Explained Ep 2

posts.caption:
Your leads are probably living in five places right now: a spreadsheet, a WhatsApp chat, a sticky note, someone's inbox and a stack of visiting cards.

Zoho CRM puts them in one place and follows each one from the first call to the closed deal. Six stations on the line:

1. Lead capture: web forms, email and calls, straight into the CRM
2. Contacts & accounts: every call, email and meeting on one timeline
3. Deal pipeline: move deals stage by stage and see what is likely to close
4. Workflow automation: rules assign leads, send follow-ups and create tasks
5. Reports & forecasts: dashboards plus where the quarter is heading
6. Zia: Zoho's AI assistant for questions, predictions and suggestions

It connects across Zoho: Campaigns for email, SalesIQ for live chat, Desk for support, Books for invoices.

By the numbers (zoho.com/crm, Nov 2026): 350,000+ businesses, 1,200+ integrations, 21 years in the making.

Practical tip: start with one pipeline and two or three automations. Add more once your team trusts the data.

Episode 2 of Zoho Explained. Next: Bigin.

Pipelines, contacts, email and WhatsApp on the deal, call logging, simple workflows and a mobile app, plus connections to Zoho Books, Campaigns, Desk and Analytics.

posts.title: Bigin by Zoho CRM explained | Zoho Explained Ep 3

posts.caption:
Not every business needs a big CRM. Some just need to stop losing deals.

Bigin is Zoho's CRM built for small businesses, and it's centred on one thing: the pipeline. Six stations on its line:

1. Pipelines: every deal in a visible stage, with more than one pipeline if you need it
2. Contacts & companies: everyone you sell to, linked to their deals
3. Email & WhatsApp: conversations tracked on the contact or deal
4. Calls: call logging on mobile, plus AI call transcripts
5. Workflows: email sequences, scheduled actions, task assignment
6. Mobile app: iOS and Android

It connects to Zoho Books, Campaigns, Desk and Analytics.

By the numbers (bigin.com, Nov 2026): 50,000+ businesses, a forever-free plan for one user, and a 15-day free trial on paid editions.

Tip: start simple. Zoho positions Zoho CRM as the upgrade path when you outgrow Bigin.

posts.title: Zoho Books explained | Zoho Explained Ep 4

posts.caption:
Month end shouldn't mean a week of typing in bank statements.

Zoho Books is Zoho's online accounting app, and Zoho lists editions for 18 countries, each built around that country's tax setup. Six stations on its line:

1. Invoices & quotes: professional quotes and invoices, with automatic payment reminders
2. Online payments: payment links on invoices
3. Bank reconciliation: match each bank line to your books
4. Bills & expenses: what you owe, tracked, and client expenses added to invoices
5. Projects & time: timesheets and a timer, billed to clients
6. Reports & tax: profit and loss, cash flow and tax reports, which can be scheduled

It connects to Zoho Expense, Billing, Inventory and Payroll.

From zoho.com/books (Nov 2026): 18 country editions, a 14-day free trial, and a free plan for small and micro businesses.

Tip: reconcile weekly, not quarterly. Small piles are easy; big piles hide mistakes.

Episode 4 of Zoho Explained. Next: Zoho Inventory.

posts.title: Zoho Inventory

posts.caption:
Selling online and in a shop? Episode 5 of Zoho Explained looks at Zoho Inventory: one stock count across warehouses and channels, serial and batch tracking, barcodes, purchase orders, packing and shipping, and reorder alerts.

It connects to Amazon, eBay, Walmart, Etsy, Shopify and WooCommerce, plus Zoho Books, CRM, Commerce and Analytics. There's a free plan for 50 orders a month (zoho.com/inventory, Nov 2026).

Next episode: Zoho Invoice.
posts.title: Zoho Inventory explained | Zoho Explained Ep 5

posts.caption:
Sold out on your website while twenty boxes sit in the back room? Or the reverse: selling something you don't have?

Zoho Inventory keeps one live stock count, updated by every purchase and every sale, across channels. Six stations on its line:

1. Multiple warehouses: stock by location, transfer orders, picklists, bin locations
2. Serial & batch tracking: trace any unit or batch to the customer who received it
3. Barcodes: generate and scan, plus RFID support
4. Purchase orders: order, receive, pay vendors; backorders and dropshipments
5. Pack & ship: packages, carriers like UPS, FedEx and DHL, post-shipment tracking
6. Reorder points: low-stock alerts before you run out

Channels: Amazon, eBay, Walmart, Etsy, Shopify, WooCommerce and Zoho Commerce.
It connects to Zoho Books, CRM, Commerce and Analytics.

From zoho.com/inventory (Nov 2026): a free plan with 50 orders a month, five plans in total, and a 14-day free trial.

Tip: do one careful stock count before you switch. Software is only as accurate as the number you start with.

Episode 5 of Zoho Explained. Next: Zoho Invoice.
